state.result: A length-preserving equiangular curvature-minus-one polygon lift has probability zero under every simplex density at positive algebraic perimeter, including P=12g.
state.scope: Fixed 120-degree corners only; variable angles, changed lengths, alternate geometric correspondences and approximate correction remain open.
state.independent_review: required at full candidate or final five-turn freeze

state.result: A closed geodesic polygon cannot have both positive algebraic side lengths and entirely algebraic angle cosines; fixed algebraic-perimeter continuous laws also almost surely avoid every such angle profile.
state.scope: Applies to exact algebraic-length lifts of finite rescaled map cores and equal-sharing angle rules. Free real angles, changed lengths, approximate correction and the source geometric law remain open.

state.result: Classical regular-polygon lift produces smooth hyperbolic surfaces, but a credited triangle-group systole bound gives a persistent short-geodesic count-law gap greater than 3/19 from the source Weil-Petersson limit, for every input-map law.
state.scope: A statement about this fixed regular geometry only, not all geometric adaptations or Gromov-Hausdorff couplings.

state.result: Angle-independent intrinsic-disk isoperimetric bound rules out exact perimeter-12g direct one-face smooth hyperbolic realizations for g>=12, with unavoidable asymptotic relative perimeter increase at least pi/3-1.
state.scope: Direct cellular geodesic realization with curvature -1; no broad geometric-bijection or weak-coupling impossibility.

state.result: An exact Dirichlet top-k mean gives uniform adaptive sparse-repair probability bounds and a necessary expected-stretch lower bound. Bounded-factor changes on o(g) edges cannot supply the direct-realization perimeter increase with nonvanishing probability.
state.remaining_gap: A geometric Chapuy adaptation with the controlled random-surface comparison sought by the source is not constructed or universally excluded.

first_observation.head: 212d6c498026765966bbe01ebe3ea09a76bb215f
first_observation.title: 30006025: reviewed geometric-Chapuy partials; original unsolved (5/5)
first_observation.body:
Accept this independently audited packet as an **unsolved partial result, 5/5 author turns**, for30006025 / OWR-14298589-010. Louf's original OWR41/2024 Question4 on printed2405 asks for a geometric adaptation of Chapuy's bijection to construct random surfaces. Its broader construction and random-surface law remain unresolved; no unrestricted impossibility or historical novelty is claimed.

The accepted partials are the specified analytic equiangular and algebraic-angle holonomy obstructions; the credited smooth regular-polygon/dessin lift with a persistent Weil–Petersson short-geodesic discrepancy; the angle-independent intrinsic perimeter bound P≥4π√(g(g−1)), excluding direct source-perimeter12g smooth one-face realizations for every g≥12; and the adaptive Dirichlet sparse-repair bounds. The latter require unchanged unselected edges and bounded multiplicative stretch. Geometric sufficiency, unrestricted real angle choices, other metric correspondences, dense/unbounded alterations and general Gromov–Hausdorff comparisons remain outside these conclusions. Matching a short-curve intensity does not identify two complete random-surface laws.

Root and four independent reviewers read primary sources and sealed mathematical reconstructions before code, outputs, final summaries or earlier/sibling verdicts. Complete author outputs reproduce byte-exactly (15,618 assertions), as do the historical independent controls (24,692). Four distinct fresh finite-control programs and the new geometric counterexamples were independently reproduced; they supplement universal proofs and credited inputs. Existing Chapuy/CFF, dessin geometry, transcendence, triangle-group classification, Poisson limit, intrinsic isoperimetry and the Dirichlet law retain their attribution.

Historical source provenance has a recorded limit: nine of ten required primary PDF identities freshly reproduce; the published Cambridge download has variable IP/time decoration and differs from its unavailable historical copy. Its actual used mathematical statements were directly checked. Historical text/raster identities are only partly reproduced. The old review's all-27 source-binding claim is attributed to that historical review and is not newly certified; no claim that every PDF byte difference is footer-only is made.

All46 original target artifacts and the five author checkpoints remain intact. The queue refresh changes only this problem's status/turn cells to unsolved5/5 against actual current main. Acceptance requires complete exact-head, literal-body, path/blob/mode, manifest, source-evidence and current-main/test-merge checks, including late stability checks and actual merge readback.

This is extensively AI-assisted research and adversarial review, unrefereed and not human peer reviewed. Per the requested process for unsolved findings, publish in the repository only: no paper, preprint, Zenodo deposit, DOI, spreadsheet entry or GitHub release.
